dependent_variable.name: D(DKVCOMP)
dependent_variable.definition: Post-minus-pre change in DKVCOMP, the De Franco-based comparability measure. Firm-specific earnings-on-return coefficients predict earnings for firm i and peer firm j using firm i’s return. Within each period, country, peer-country, and industry cell, the signed measure is minus the average absolute prediction difference across available firm pairs; n_{p,ci,cj,k} is that available-pair count. For same-country comparisons (ci=cj), the paper excludes i=j self-pairs. Higher, less negative values indicate greater comparability. Equation (3) displays the outcome label DVKCOMP, while adjacent prose and Table 2 call the measure DKVCOMP.

evidence.quote: Equation (3) prints DVKCOMP_p,ci,cj,k = -sum_i,j abs(alpha_p,i,0 + alpha_p,i,1*RET_p,i - (alpha_p,j,0 + alpha_p,j,1*RET_p,i))/n_p,ci,cj,k.
DKVCOMP is a comparability measure based on De Franco et al. (2011), where firm-to-firm comparability is assessed by the similarity of firm-level earnings on return regressions.
For both measures, larger (less negative) values indicate more comparable financial accounting information.
n_p,ci,cj,k is the number of available firm pairs within industry k, with i from country ci and j from country cj; when ci=cj, the PDF explicitly requires i != j.

evidence.quote: We define GAAP_PROX as the negative number of differences divided by the maximum number of differences observed across all country pairs
IFRS_EFFECT captures the change in GAAP_PROX caused by the adoption of IFRS in the treatment countries.
To capture this relation, our main treatment variable is the change of GAAP_PROX between the 2004 and 2008 periods (IFRS_EFFECT).
If both countries are the same, GAAP_PROX takes the value of zero, i.e., the maximum value of GAAP proximity.

Since the adoption of IFRS has affected the GAAP of some treatment countries to become more dissimilar relative to some control countries, values of the IFRS_EFFECT can be negative as well as positive.

Throughout the analysis higher values of our measures indicate that the financial accounting information of the two respective countries for a given period and industry are more comparable with each other.

CFCOMP is a similar construct, where firm-to-firm comparability is assessed by the similarity of firm-level total accruals on cash flow regressions.
For both measures, larger (less negative) values indicate more comparable financial accounting information.

independent_variables.definition: The IFRS-induced change in GAAP_PROX for the country pair. GAAP_PROX is the negative number of GAAP differences between the two countries divided by the maximum number of differences observed across all country pairs; same-country pairs have GAAP_PROX=0. evidence.quote: We define GAAP_PROX as the negative number of differences divided by the maximum number of differences observed across all country pairs
IFRS_EFFECT captures the change in GAAP_PROX caused by the adoption of IFRS in the treatment countries.
To capture this relation, our main treatment variable is the change of GAAP_PROX between the 2004 and 2008 periods (IFRS_EFFECT).
If both countries are the same, GAAP_PROX takes the value of zero, i.e., the maximum value of GAAP proximity.

Since the adoption of IFRS has affected the GAAP of some treatment countries to become more dissimilar relative to some control countries, values of the IFRS_EFFECT can be negative as well as positive.

review_notes: Principal family: Model (6), Table 2 Panel B, the first-difference IFRS treatment test, with separate outcomes D(DKVCOMP), D(R_DKVCOMP), D(CFCOMP), and D(R_CFCOMP). The abstract and introduction identify the effect of mandatory IFRS adoption on accounting comparability as the central question; the pre-IFRS Model (5) is an identification check and the compliance, moderation, information-transfer, and private-firm analyses are follow-up questions.

Equations (1) and (2) are retained as supporting fits because their firm-period coefficients construct the two underlying comparability measures used in Model (6). The supplied verified transcription identifies these equations and the mathematical forms of Equations (3), (4), and (6); the extraction uses that supplied derivative without self-certifying its math.

The paper does not identify the underlying estimator for Model (6) or the two repeated firm-period measurement fits. The signed direction of the rank transformation is not printed, although the paper says higher values of its measures indicate more comparability. Table 2 reports robust standard errors clustered by country, peer-country, and industry, but does not establish whether these are joint or separate multi-way clusters.

Equation (3) labels its outcome DVKCOMP, while the adjacent prose and Table 2 label the measure DKVCOMP. The extraction follows the prose/table outcome name and preserves the notation discrepancy here. Equation (6) omits a separate ordinary-intercept symbol, while Table 2 reports an Intercept row; the table supports an included intercept.

The level measures and GAAP_PROX are retained as components/raw inputs to the selected change outcomes and IFRS_EFFECT.
